title: Build your own private file-sharing site with an agent
summary: A founder asked his Hermes agent over Telegram to build a WeTransfer-style file sharing site on his own domain; he says it works, with codes, expiry and upload alerts.
agent_role: The agent first shared files straight from the owner's Mac on request, then set up a subdomain and built the sharing service. The human gave the request and set the requirements.
outcome: Author reports a working share site with per-link 6-digit codes, auto-deletion, 5 GB client uploads and Telegram alerts, free up to 10 GB.
what_they_did: The poster runs an agent called Mero on Hermes, which he messages through Telegram. When a developer needed a client's raw videos, Mero shared them directly from his Mac over the team's private network. That night he had Mero set up a share subdomain and build a file-transfer site on Cloudflare.
how_it_went: He says each share gets its own link and 6-digit code, files delete after a time he picks, clients can upload up to 5 GB, and he gets a Telegram ping on opens and uploads.
worth_knowing: The author admits it may be abandoned within a week; a home-built tool still needs someone to keep it running.
prompt: Build me a private file-sharing site on [your domain] using [hosting service, e.g. Cloudflare]. Each share should get its own link and a 6-digit access code. Let me set how long each share lives, then delete the files automatically. Let clients upload files up to [size limit]. Send me a message on [Telegram or email] when someone opens or uploads. Show me your plan and expected costs first, and wait for my approval before changing my domain settings or deploying.

curation.rationale: A concrete case of a messaging-controlled agent building and deploying a private file-sharing service overnight, with specific features. It is self-reported with no code or demo.
